texts.preamble: Date Of Decision: 7.8.2024 vs Prem Singh And Another on 7 August, 2024 Author: Sandeep Sharma Bench: Sandeep Sharma 2024:Hhc:6 In The High Court Of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla Criminal Revision Petition No. 129 of 2022 . Date of Decision: 7.8.2024 _____________________________________________________________________ State of Himachal Pradesh .........Petitio Versus Prem Singh and another .......Respondents Coram Hon'ble Mr. Justice Sandeep Sharma, Judge. Whether approved for reporting? __ _ _ _ _ _ _ __ __ __ _ __ Date Of Decision: 7.8.2024 vs Prem Singh And Another on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173147463/ 1 Sandeep Sharma, J. (Oral)
texts.facts: In the instant proceedings filed under Section 397 read with Section 401 of CrPC, challenge has been laid to order dated 19.10.2021, passed by the learned Special Judge, Mandi, District Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, whereby challan submitted by the police against the respondents, for their having committed offence punishable under Sections 406, 411 & 120-B of Indian Penal Code (in short the "IPC") and under Sections 4 & 7 of Himachal Pradesh Prevention of Specific Corrupt Practices Act, 1983 (in short the "Act"), came to be returned on the ground that same is not presented to the court by the authorized officer. 2. Precisely, the facts of the case as emerge from the record are that person namely Amar Singh i.e. respondent No.2, who at the relevant time, was a Government Contractor, unauthorizedly sold the bags of 2 2024:HHC:6779 cement issued to him by the Public Works Department for construction of Government property to a private person namely Prem Singh i.e. . respondent No.1. Police, after being submitted report by the Executive Engineer B&R Division, HPPWD, Gohar, registered FIR against the respondents under Sections 406, 411 and 120-B of IPC and under Sections 4 & 7 of the Act. After completion of investigation, police presented challan in the competent court of law i.e. learned Special Judge, Mandi, District Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, under the aforesaid provisions of law. 3. Vide impugned order dated 19.10.2021, learned Special Judge while discharging the accused named in the challan returned the challan to the police reserving liberty to the prosecution to submit report to the court on the prescribed proforma made by the authorized officer as per rules, if so advised. 4. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with impugned order dated 19.10.2021, petitioner-State has come before this Court in the instant proceedings, praying therein to [LEAKAGE_MASK] aforesaid order.
texts.arguments: 5. Precisely, the grouse of the petitioner, as has been highlighted in the petition and further canvassed by Mr. B.C. Verma, learned Additional Advocate General, is that since very basis of FIR, on the basis of which, challan under Section 173 CrPC came to be submitted in the court of learned Special Judge Mandi, was the report submitted by the Executive Engineer B&R Division, HPPWD, Gohar, who is competent authority under 3 2024:HHC:6779 Section 36 of the Act, there was no occasion, if any, for the learned Special Judge to return the finding that report was not submitted by the competent . authority as prescribed under Section 36 of the afore Act. Mr. Verma, further submitted that otherwise also, there is no bar, if any, under Section 30 of the Act to take cognizance on the basis of police report, which otherwise in the present case was on the basis of report submitted by the Executive Engineer B&R Division, HPPWD, Gohar, who was competent authority under Section 36 of the Act, to make a report in writing to the court. To substantiate his aforesaid submission, Mr. Verma, specifically invited attention of this Court to judgment dated 4.11.2022, passed by coordinate Bench of this Court in Case titled State of Himachal Pradesh v. Labh Singh and Anr., in Date Of Decision: 7.8.2024 vs Prem Singh And Another on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173147463/ 2 Criminal Revision No. 151 of 2022. 6. To the contrary, Mr. G.R. Palsra, Advocate, appearing for the respondents, while supporting the impugned order, submitted that once Section 36 of the Act clearly provides that no court would take contingence of the offence under this Act against any person, unless a report in writing is made by an officer not below the rank of an Under Secretary, no illegality can be said to have been committed by the learned Special Judge while returning the challan because admittedly, same was not submitted to the court by the competent authority in terms of Section 36, rather same was presented by the police, which was not competent to do so. 4 2024:HHC:6779 7. At this stage, it would be apt to take note of Section 36 of the Act, which reads as under: "36. Cognizance of offences- No court shall take cognizance of an offence under this Act against any person unless a report in writing is made by such an officer not below the rank of a 1 [Under Secretary] as the State Government as it may by a notification, specify: Provided that no such report shall be made against a member of judicial service of State saves with the prior concurrence of the High Court. 8. Aforesaid provision of law clearly talks about prohibition of cognizable offences under the Act by any court, unless a report in writing is made 5 2024:HHC:6779 by the authorized officer to be notified by the State Government. As per aforesaid provision of law, Authorized Officer should not below the rank of Under Secretary. . 9. The question, which needs determination at the first instance, is "whether making of report is to be construed a report being made to the Court by the Authorized Officer as a pre-condition for taking of cognizance or Authorized Officer at the first instance would make report to the police enabling it to investigate the matter and file challan, if any, in the competent court of law". Date Of Decision: 7.8.2024 vs Prem Singh And Another on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173147463/ 3 10. To explore answer to aforesaid query posed by this Court, it would be apt to take note of Section 39 of CrPC, which reads as under: "39. Public to give information of certain offences. (1) Every person aware of the commission of, or of the intention of any other person to commit, any offence punishable under any of the following sections of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860), namely - (i) Sections 121 to 126, both inclusive, and section 130 (that is to say, offences against the State specified in Chapter VI of the said Code); (ii) Sections 143, 144, 145, 147 and 148 (that is to say, offences against the public tranquillity specified in Chapter VIII of the said Code); (iii) Sections 161 to 165-A, both inclusive (that is to say, offences relating to illegal gratification); (iv) Sections 272 to 278 both inclusive (that is to say, offences relating to adulteration of food and drugs, etc.), (v) Sections 302, 303 and 304 (that is to say, offences affecting life); (va) [ Section 364A (that is to say, offence relating to kidnapping for ransom, etc.) [Inserted by Act 42 of 1993, Section 3 (w.e.f. 22-5-1993).] 6 2024:HHC:6779 (vi) Section 382 (that is to say, offence of theft after preparation made for causing death, hurt or restraint in order to the . committing of the theft); (vii) Sections 392 to 399, both inclusive, and section 402 (that is to say, offences of robbery and dacoity); (viii) Section 409 (that is to say, offence relating to criminal breach of trust by public servant, etc.); (ix) Sections 431 to 439, both inclusive (that is to say, offences of mischief against property); (x) Sections 449 and 450 (that is to say, offences of house- trespass); (xi) Sections 456 to 460, both inclusive (that is to say, offences of lurking house-trespass); and (xii) Sections 489-A to 489-E, both inclusive (that is to say, offences relating to currency notes and bank notes), shall in the absence of any reasonable excuse, the burden of proving which excuse shall lie upon the person so aware, forthwith give information to the nearest Magistrate or police officer of such commission or intention. Date Of Decision: 7.8.2024 vs Prem Singh And Another on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173147463/ 4 (2) For the purposes of this section, the term "offence" includes any act committed at any place out of India which would constitute an offence if committed in India." 11. As per aforesaid provision of law, every person aware of the commission of, or of the intention of any other person to commit, any offence punishable under any of the sections of the IPC, as detailed in the aforesaid provision of law, shall give information to the nearest Magistrate or police officer of such commission or intention. 12. Section 190 of Cr.PC, further empowers the Magistrate to cognizance of any offence; (a) upon receiving a complaint of facts which constitute such offence; (b) upon a police report of such fact and; (c) upon information received 7 2024:HHC:6779 from any person other than a police officer or upon his own knowledge that such offence has been committed. . 13. Section 173 CrPC deals with police report, sub-clause 2 whereof makes it mandatory for the officer in charge of the Police Station concerned to file charge sheet on completion of investigation before the Magistrate empowered to take cognizance of the offence. 14. In the case at hand, learned Special Judge while passing impugned order has held that police has obtained a report from the Executive Engineer B&R Division, Gohar, in which it was mentioned that Executive Engineer is the competent authority under Section 36 of the Act, to make a writing to the court, that accused Amar Singh should be prosecuted in the court of law for commission 8 2024:HHC:6779 of the offence. At this stage, it would be apt to take note of 36A of the Act, which reads as under: 9 2024:HHC:6779 "[36-A. Investigation of offences.- Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974), in case of a public servant, no . Police Officer below the rank of the Deputy Superintendent of Police shall investigate into or make any arrest in, an offence punishable under this Act: [Provided that the State Government may, by general or specific order, authorize a police officer not below the rank of Inspector of Police to investigate into, or make any arrest in, an offence punishable under this Act.] Explanation.-For the purpose of this section "public servant" means a public servant as defined in 2 [clause (c) of section 2 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.]" In similar facts and circumstances, coordinate Bench of this Court Labh Singh (supra) has held as under: . "13.
